key_decisions: The op-group removal was scoped to the DATA + the UI, not the resolver. The resolver's op axis (hasOperationGroups, selectableOps, expandRequiredOps, dependentsOfOp, the operations branches in resolveDeps/deriveInstalledOps) and the backend uninstall guard that calls it in BOTH engine twins (routes/downloadManager.js, MPI-310) are left standing. Nothing ships the shape, so they return empty for every real model — but ripping them out is a change to shared-dep PROTECTION with its own bug history, and doing that in the same pass as three unrelated fixes was the wrong trade. It is dead-but-correct, and the tests cover it with synthetic models. The user has been told and can ask for it.

isOperationInstalled's supportedOps guard is the load-bearing part of the flatten and the easiest thing to undo by accident. The flat branch used to ignore its `op` argument entirely — it answered isModelUsable — so flattening wan-22 without it would have silently reversed MPI-453 for legacy t2v history items.

minVramGb is per-model, NOT a change to K or MIN_FLOOR in footprint.js, which would re-floor the whole library. And only an explicit override draws an off-grid row: the first cut let the COMPUTED floor draw one too and put '8.28951171875GB min' on Wan's card. That was caught by probing the live drawer, not by a test — the self-check now pins every row to the 8GB grid when no override is set.

The tier letter gates on `name`, not `modelFamily`. modelFamily groups models that are merely related (Wan-2.2 holds 'Wan 2.2 Smooth' + 'Wan 2.2 5B'; MiniMax-H3 holds 'MiniMax H3' + 'MiniMax H3 Reference') — distinct names, so the letter disambiguated nothing. It is also install-gated now, which means a gallery card made by a tier whose sibling is uninstalled shows a bare name. That reverses a deliberate earlier decision ('a gallery asset should always show which tier made it'), on the user's explicit call.

MPI-476 was carded separately from MPI-475 rather than folded into it. MPI-475 is a model-wiring card with its own unmet gates; these were four independent surface drifts the user reported while reviewing it.
